title: The locate cache reads a byte buffer back as T without regard to alignment or byte order
body:
`SufrFile::set_suffix_array_mem` in `libsufr/src/sufr_file.rs` reads the rank section of the cache file into a `Vec<u8>` and turns it into ranks with:

```rust
std::slice::from_raw_parts(buffer.as_ptr() as *const _, suffix_array_len).to_vec()
```

A `Vec<u8>` only guarantees an alignment of 1. Building a `&[T]` from that pointer is undefined behaviour when `T` is `u32` or `u64` and the allocation is not aligned for it. Common allocators happen to return aligned blocks, so this probably works in practice.

The cache stores every value in native byte order, through `u64::from_ne_bytes` and the raw slice casts. A cache written on one architecture and read on another of the other endianness yields wrong values. That matters only if a cache directory is shared between machines.

Found by reading the code. Not reproduced.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4be42394
notes.text:
At cff9fb6 the cache read fills a `Vec<T>` through `as_bytes_mut` (`index.rs:304-327`, `io.rs:222-232`). The `Vec<u8>` to `&[T]` cast and its alignment problem are gone.

The byte order problem remains. Suffix and rank data are still written and read in native byte order (TODOs at `io.rs:220` and `io.rs:234`). Only the length prefix is little-endian (`index.rs:310`, `index.rs:590`).
